name: Crib Point
intro: Crib Point sits halfway between Hastings and Stony Point on the Western Port shoreline, a small village built around a navy history that quietly defined it for most of the twentieth century  -  HMAS Cerberus is its southern neighbour and the largest naval base in the country. The village is residential, with a station on the Stony Point train line and a few low-key streets that lead down to Woolleys Beach, a small shaded swimming pocket that locals know about and almost no visitors do. The Western Port coast here is mangrove and mudflat country, and walking south along the foreshore toward Stony Point at low tide is one of the better long, flat coastal walks on the Peninsula. Come here for the walks and the train; stay in Hastings for the meal.
factualLede: Crib Point is a small residential village on the Mornington Peninsula's Western Port coast between Hastings and Stony Point, 80 km from Melbourne, with a station on the Stony Point train line and Woolleys Beach on the foreshore.

heroImage.alt: Mangroves and a wooden walkway at Woolleys Beach near Crib Point

tldr: Crib Point is the small residential village between Hastings and Stony Point — Woolleys Beach, a train station and a long foreshore walk toward the ferry.
Best for: walkers; carless travellers; people building the Western Port loop properly.
Signature experience: low-tide walk south along the foreshore toward Stony Point, ferry on, train back.
Half a day; pair with Hastings or Stony Point for a full day.
There is little to eat in the village — provision in Hastings.
signature: The walking village between Hastings and the Stony Point ferry — quiet, mangrove-edged, train-accessible.
skip: Looking for a meal — eat in Hastings and walk in Crib Point.
bestDay: Train to Crib Point from Frankston, low-tide foreshore walk south to Stony Point, ferry to French Island or back, train home.
insiderNote: The Stony Point line is the only train that runs onto the Peninsula's Western Port side — Crib Point is the quietest stop with the best foreshore access.
